How is my vision?

Blurred or hard-to-read vision. Tell the medical officer today.

Why it happens: Fluid shift can press on the back of the eye and change near vision on long stays.

Try:
• Repeat the vision check one eye at a time.
• Write down when it started and what you see.
• Tell the medical officer today.

Call for help: Sooner if it is sudden, one-sided or comes with flashes or a severe headache.

This is guidance, not a diagnosis.

What should I eat?

Astronaut Nutrition & Dietary Guidelines:

• Caloric Target: ~2,800 to 3,200 kcal/day (adjusted for body mass and 2.5 hours of daily resistive exercise).
• Sodium Restriction: Keep sodium under 2,000 mg/day. High sodium exacerbates fluid retention and elevates intracranial/ocular pressure (SANS).
• Bone Support: Vitamin D3 (800-1000 IU/day) and Calcium (1,000-1,200 mg/day) are supplemented daily due to lack of solar ultraviolet exposure.
• Packaging: All meals are thermostabilized, irradiated, or freeze-dried. Ensure full rehydration with warm potable water before eating to avoid gastrointestinal discomfort.

I feel nauseous

Nausea or dizziness. Monitor and log it.

Why it happens: Space adaptation in the first days, or balance changes after gravity returns. Also high CO₂.

Try:
• Move your head slowly and fix your eyes on a still point.
• Sit or lie down and drink water.
• Log when it happens.

Call for help: If you faint, vomit for over a day or have chest pain.

This is guidance, not a diagnosis.

What can you do?

I am the Autonomous Medical Decision Support Assistant.

I can:
• Read your live vitals (Heart rate, Blood pressure, SpO₂, Temp, Respiration, HRV)
• Monitor cabin atmosphere (CO₂, Pressure, ppO₂, Radiation)
• Track long-term risks (Bone density, Muscle mass, SANS vision, Sleep debt, Hydration)
• Triage symptoms and explain flight medical protocols
• Provide guidance on sleep, nutrition, exercise, hygiene, and space adaptation

I operate 100% offline aboard your craft, and can also connect online via Google Gemini AI when comms are open.

Is my radiation dose safe?

Radiation Protection & Cabin Shielding:

• Live Cabin Dose Rate: 75 µSv/h.
• Cumulative Mission Exposure: 16 % of reference.
• Environmental Sources: Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCRs) provide steady background radiation, while Solar Particle Events (SPEs) pose sudden acute risks.

Behavioral Health & Mission Wellness:

• Long-duration spaceflight imposes severe sensory deprivation, confinement, and crew isolation.
• Daily Strategies:
  1. Maintain structured personal time and daily journaling.
  2. Stay connected with family and ground support via private communication links.
  3. Exercise regularly—endorphins combat confinement stress.
  4. Practice mindfulness or breathing cycles if feeling anxious or claustrophobic.
• Private Medical Conferences (PMCs) with the Mission Flight Psychologist are available confidentially. You are never alone on this mission.
